newsitem.title: GERMANY: German crafts, trades say left out of recovery.
newsitem.headline: German crafts, trades say left out of recovery.

text.p: Germany's butchers, bakers and candlestick makers have been passed over by the rebound in the economy, the ZDH federation of skilled crafts and tradesmen said on Thursday.

The trades, employing around seven million skilled workers with turnover last year of 1.0 trillion marks ($667.2 billion), have not benefitted from economic recovery. They also see business stagnating in 1997 and expect firms to cut jobs, the federation said.

"We, in the trades, cannot expect fundamental improvement next year," ZDH general secretary Hanns-Eberhard Schleyer told reporters in Bonn. "Even after considering the effects of seasonal changes, the situation for the trades is serious."
In western Germany, 34 percent of respondents to a ZDH survey said they expected business to worsen this year, while just 14 percent expect improvement.
In eastern Germany, where firms have been hit hard by the slump in the building sector, a majority of respondents were pessimistic about future developments.
The trades have also been hit by falling public investment as Germany's cash-strapped municipal authorities curb spending.
